name: thin_stroke_preservation_v1
description: Train from SCRATCH with rebalanced loss weights optimized for thin stroke preservation (pixel=100, adv=1.0, perceptual=2.0)
strategy: Train from scratch with optimal loss balance discovered from dataset analysis (44% thin strokes available)

dataset.description: 4.7GB synthetic paleography dataset with 44.14% thin strokes (<3px)

training.description: Full training (50 epochs ~10-15 hours) from scratch with loss weights optimized for thin stroke preservation based on dataset analysis showing 44% thin stroke representation

generator.description: Standard LR for training from scratch

discriminator.description: Standard LR for training from scratch

loss_weights.description: CRITICAL CHANGES: pixel 50→100 (+2x preserve detail), adv 3.0→1.0 (-3x reduce aggression), perceptual 1.0→2.0 (+2x maintain structure)

rationale.pixel_increase: Force generator to preserve ALL pixels including thin strokes
rationale.adv_decrease: Make discriminator less punishing for keeping thin strokes (previously treated as noise)
rationale.perceptual_increase: Maintain overall structure quality while preserving fine details

model.description: Same architecture as production_v3 - only loss weights changed

experiment_metadata.hypothesis: Dataset has 44% thin strokes but production_v3 lost 56.6% of them due to adversarial loss too high (3.0). Training from scratch with balanced losses (pixel=100, adv=1.0, perceptual=2.0) should preserve >75% thin strokes.
experiment_metadata.success_criteria: Thin stroke preservation 43.4% → >75% while maintaining PSNR ≥16 dB and F-Measure ≥98%
experiment_metadata.rationale: Training from scratch is BETTER than fine-tuning because: (1) Dataset already has sufficient thin strokes (44%), (2) Optimizer state incompatibility with new LR, (3) Model will learn correct objective from epoch 0
